Coverage of the compiled code of R

Source: R/base_r_compiled.R
base_r_compiled_coverage.Rd

Computes the coverage of the C, C++ and Fortran code of R itself, from the counts that gcov records while R runs, e.g. under make check. This is for measuring R, not packages: use package_coverage() for those.

Usage

base_r_compiled_coverage(
  build_dir,
  source_dir,
  exclude = "tests",
  cores = 1L,
  batch_size = 50L,
  quiet = TRUE,
  gcov_path = resolve_gcov(),
  gcov_args = getOption("covr.gcov_args", NULL)
)

Arguments

build_dir

The directory R was configured and built in, after the counts were collected.

source_dir

The directory with the R sources it was built from.

exclude

Directories relative to source_dir whose files are left out of the coverage.

cores

The number of parallel processes to run gcov in. Forking is not available on Windows.

batch_size

The number of objects gcov is run on at a time.

quiet

Whether to hide the progress messages.

gcov_path

The path of the gcov executable.

gcov_args

Extra arguments for gcov.

Value

A coverage object of the lines of the files in source_dir, with absolute file names.

Details

All objects with a .gcno file are measured, also if no process ran them and no .gcda file was written, so their lines count as not covered. gcov is run in a temporary directory, in batches of batch_size objects that may run in cores parallel processes, so neither the build nor the source tree get any files. Headers outside of source_dir, and generated files in the build tree, are dropped.

Requirements

  • R must be built from source, out of tree, with --coverage in the compiler flags, e.g. CFLAGS="-O0 --coverage" FFLAGS="-O0 --coverage" LDFLAGS=--coverage. Every object in build_dir then has a .gcno file with its layout, and processes of that R write .gcda files of counts when they exit.

  • gcov must be available, see covr.gcov in covr-package.

  • Processes forked by parallel::mclapply() leave with _exit() and don't write their gcov counts, unless R code was instrumented by instrument_base_r() on a build with --coverage.

  • This is only supported on Unix-alikes.

Example workflow

# Build R with coverage flags in `build_dir` from the sources in
# `source_dir`, and run its checks: `make check`
cov <- base_r_compiled_coverage("build", "R-devel", cores = 4)
report(cov)

See also

The article Coverage of R itself.
